title: per-route slab rebalance misattribution during burst-window handoff
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
During large-burst rebalance operations that move slabed burst credits between per-route buckets, we observed credits being transiently assigned to the wrong route shard which allowed a short window of silent-allow behavior. The underlying code attempts a non-atomic two-step transfer (debit source slab -> temp holding -> credit target slab), and under concurrent handoffs the temp holding record can be lost or merged into the wrong route key if a race occurs.

Observed impact:
- Small percentage of requests (~0.3-0.8%) in a 24h window were served without decrementing the originating route's quota; customers with tight per-route SLAs saw spiky allowance.
- Billing vs. enforcement drift: downstream metering pipeline omitted some of the temp-hold transitions, causing reconciliation reports to undercount usage for a subset of routes for affected orgs.

Hypothesis / root cause:
- Non-atomic transfer of burst credits during slab rebalance between route shards.
- Hash-collision / namespace remapping during rebalance can cause the temp-holder key to be garbage-collected into an adjacent shard in the presence of a concurrent shard-split event.
- Integer truncation when computing slab slice sizes caused off-by-one assignments, making the timing window where temp-holder exists longer than intended.

Reproduction steps (dev environment):
1) Create two routes under one org with small per-route burst slab sizes (e.g., 50 credits).
2) Rapidly send interleaved high-rate requests hitting route-A then route-B to force rebalance code path.
3) Trigger controlled shard-split (provoker script in test harness) while transfers are in-flight.
4) Observe via test harness logs that temp-holder key is sometimes reassigned to route-C (another test route) or disappears.

Relevant logs / traces:
- Example span: trace_id=01f3a... slab_rebalance.start -> slab_rebalance.transfer(temp_key=org:123:tmp:shard-7) -> slab_rebalance.commit.
- Metrics: slab.transfer_in_flight_peak=24, slab.temp_key_evictions=7 over 1h window.

Immediate mitigation suggested:
- Short-term: Disable automatic cross-shard slab rebalance for orgs with per-route slabs until fix is deployed (config flag per-org: slab_rebalance.enabled=false). This reduces flexibility but stops the silent-allow window.
- Monitoring: Add a realtime alert for slab.temp_key_evictions > 1/min for any shard.

Proposed permanent fixes:
1) Make slab transfer atomic at the storage layer (single compare-and-swap or transactional write), removing the temp-holder intermediate.
2) Change key namespace during rebalance to include monotonic rebalance-id so accidental remap collisions are impossible.
3) Tighten integer math when slicing slabs; add unit tests for boundary conditions (N mod M cases).
4) Add reconciliation job (one-off migration) to detect and re-credit any lost/deferred debits and to produce a ledger of corrections for billing team.

Acceptance criteria:
- No silent-allow windows in integration test harness under 10k concurrent flows in CI.
- E2E reconciliation job runs and fixes known drift for the sample orgs used in incident test (org-123, org-546).
- Change passes security and performance review and is released in runtime-1.24.2 with rollout plan to 100% in 48h.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: runtime-1.24.2 to a single region and two non-production orgs to validate transfers under load.
- Gradual: 20% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with manual stop on alert.

comments: 2025-02-12 - Asha Patel: Filed after initial incident report from SRE team. Attached preliminary logs and metrics. Marking P1 due to potential billing/exposure.

2025-02-13 - Liu Chen: Started triage, reproduced locally with repro-harness; confirmed temp-holder evictions correlated with shard-split timing. Created test harness PR to force deterministic shard-split. https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-harness/pull/58

2025-02-15 - Priya Nair (SRE): Deployed org-level feature flag (slab_rebalance.enabled=false) for 5 suspect orgs; observed immediate stop of silent-allow spikes. Documented mitigation playbook in runbook. https://confluence.redwood/Runbooks/SlabRebalance

2025-02-18 - Diego Martinez (Eng Lead): Code review notes on runtime PR: prefer storing rebalance-id in key rather than temp-holder TTL trick. See review comments in PR #4321. Added performance benchmark requirement for atomic transfer option.

2025-02-21 - Liu Chen: Implemented atomic-transfer PoC using transactional write; initial microbench shows 4% p95 latency increase for small-slab paths, but within SLO when batching enabled. Linked benchmark results: https://perf.redwood-inference.com/bench/4321
2025-02-24 - Finance (note): Requested reconciliation ledger prior to billing cycle close; Finance Slack thread: #billing -> https://slack.redwood-inference.com/archives/C01234F56
2025-02-25 - Asha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria and added migration reconciliation job to schedule. Preparing release notes draft for runtime-1.24.2.
2025-02-25 - Liu Chen: Opened runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 (WIP). Tests added: unit+integration reproducer + reconciliation job smoke test.
postmortem_notes: Preliminary postmortem: the root cause is race during cross-shard slab transfer combined with a long-lived temp-holder that can be reclaimed into adjacent namespace due to a shard-split event. The one-off reconciliation job will enumerate temp-holder evictions and compute missing debits. We will coordinate with Finance to issue any billing adjustments for affected orgs (estimated 3-6 customers).
mitigation_actions: 1) Org-level flag to disable rebalance (done for 5 orgs). 2) Reconciliation job scheduled to run nightly and produce a correction ledger. 3) Alert rule added for slab.temp_key_evictions > 1/min.
verification_plan: Run CI integration with repro-harness at 10k concurrent flows. Validate no temp_key_evictions and that atomic transfer code paths do not regress p95 latency beyond SLA. Manually reconcile sample orgs and confirm ledger numbers match expected usage.
